links.comparator_used: Direct API access to the same chatbot models, without the UI's additional safety controls (moderation rules, crisis refusal templates, system-level instructions)
links.outcome: Proportion of responses to suicide-related prompts that directly answered the prompt (lower is safer for higher-risk prompts)
links.effect: Direct responses: 62.2% UI vs 77.4% API overall. Very-high-risk prompts: 4.6% UI vs 24.8% API. High-risk prompts: 48.4% UI vs 80.1% API. Mixed-effects OR for UI vs API 0.09 (95% CI 0.08-0.10).
links.tradeoff: The study did not isolate which UI safeguards caused the difference. The pattern was not uniform: Gemini had higher direct response rates via UI (76.7%) than API (71.0%), and access mode differences varied by risk level and model.
links.quote: In mixed-effects models, UI access was associated with lower odds of a direct response than API access (odds ratio 0.09, 95% CI 0.08-0.10).

design_hint: consumer UI safety controls (moderation, crisis refusal, system instructions) vs raw API access
